cues.text: Where the rules are clear, let the machine win.
Where there are none, that is where we work.
The Polymath Manifesto.
One. Walk into the fog, and walk out with a map:
a well-posed problem, a scope, a deadline,
and a value you can measure.
Two. Breadth needs roots.
Go deep in one or two fields, then branch out.
A conventional base plus a small dose of the unusual nearly doubled the odds of impact.
Three. Connect, don't collect.
Anyone can look things up.
The advantage is seeing that a technical problem is really about incentives,
or trust.
Four. Think in systems.
Look for feedback loops, second-order effects,
and every actor's incentives.
Ask what structure produces this result.
Five. Doubt with method.
In a test of seven hundred fifty-eight consultants,
AI lifted quality forty percent.
Outside its frontier,
accuracy fell from eighty-four to sixty or seventy percent.
Six. AI amplifies, judgment steers.
A machine can generate a thousand connections.
Choosing the one that matters, and answering for it, is on us.
Seven. The human side is half the problem.
In nineteen fifty-one,
coal mines showed that technology and people must be designed together.
Eight. Translate between worlds.
The board speaks value and risk, the engineer feasibility,
the operator daily reality.
We carry the meaning across, and we persuade.
Nine. The body and the terrain know things too.
Go where the work happens and sit beside the person doing it.
The real problem is never only in the report.
Ten. Build, and answer for it.
An idea never tested is no different from a hallucination.
We ask not just can we, but should we, and who does it affect.
Eleven. We are measured by what happens after we leave.
If people don't use it, the failure is ours.
Train, document, hand over, until the team runs without us.
Twelve. Learning is the craft.
Our only lasting edge is how fast and how well we learn.
We build small prototypes and test them with real users,
in days, not months.
Where the rules are clear, let the machine win.
Where there are none, we are there.
And when we leave, the map stays.
